parsed.explanation: Thin-data jurisdiction requiring extrapolation. Structural signals: sodomy provisions were enforced within living memory (35 arrests 1995-2000, group sentences 2001) and were only read down — not repealed — in 2024; no gender-identity protection exists; police dismissiveness toward anti-LGBT violence is documented (refusal to investigate a 2019 attack, victims ridiculed); a killing of a man perceived as gay occurred (2010, dated); religious leaders have called publicly for excluding gay tourists. No trans-specific prosecution, violence, document rule or facility rule is documented — those are open questions, not exposures, but with no documented acceptance tradition or protective machinery to offset them. No universal-exposure measure or organised targeting appears; worst documented feature is tier-3 societal hostility with thin recourse. The functioning courts that produced the 2024 ruling, the 2011 UN statement and supportive religious voices are moderate positives, but recourse for trans-specific harm is unproven and police practice is damning where documented. This sits between the 0.45 and 0.55 anchors: above jurisdictions with unremedied universal rules, below those with documented acceptance traditions and working remedies. 0.48.
